Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:

- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.

- No error handling for impossible scenarios.

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

# Code Review: `nodes/sros/sros.go` readiness command update

## Summary

The PR is a focused, three-line change to the SR-SIM (`nokia_srsim`) readiness probes in `nodes/sros/sros.go`. The readiness commands are changed from exact-name process matches to full-command-line substring matches:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `/usr/bin/pgrep ^cpm$` | `/usr/bin/pgrep -f /opt/nokia/cpm` |
| `/usr/bin/pgrep ^both$` | `/usr/bin/pgrep -f /opt/nokia/both` |
| `/usr/bin/pgrep ^iom$` | `/usr/bin/pgrep -f /opt/nokia/iom` |

This follows the intended flow: the `readyCmd*` constants are consumed only by `sros.Ready()` (`nodes/sros/sros.go:920-958`), which polls all three probes via `n.RunExec` and returns success when any one probe exits with code `0`. I verified that `NewExecCmdFromString` parses the new three-argument command string the same way it parsed the old two-argument one (`exec/exec.go:36`), and that no other code, tests, docs, or schema reference these process names or the probe commands. There is precedent in the repository for this style of probe (`nodes/spirent_stc/stc.go:71` uses `pgrep -f capture_0`), and the change matches the "surgical changes" rule — no unrelated code was touched.

## Severity summary

| Priority | Count | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 0 | — |
| P4 | 1 | Unanchored `pgrep -f` patterns can match unrelated processes |

## Finding details

### P4 — Unanchored `pgrep -f` patterns can match unrelated processes

**Location:** [nodes/sros/sros.go, lines 112–114](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/638eefdca86dd103dc518ebd37ea5826b248fe00/nodes/sros/sros.go#L112-L114)

**Problem:** The replacement patterns `/opt/nokia/cpm`, `/opt/nokia/both`, and `/opt/nokia/iom` are passed to `pgrep -f`, which matches them as unanchored extended regular expressions against each process's full command line. The prior patterns (`^cpm$`, `^both$`, `^iom$`) matched the process name exactly, so the semantic change also drops the anchoring that previously prevented collateral matches.

**Trigger:** Any process inside the SR-SIM container whose command line merely *contains* one of these path strings — for example a wrapper shell, an entrypoint script referencing the path, or a log watcher such as `tail -f /opt/nokia/cpm/...` — will satisfy the corresponding probe. `pgrep` excludes itself, so the probe process itself is not a false positive.

**Impact:** `Ready()` (`nodes/sros/sros.go:933-956`) returns success as soon as any one probe exits `0`. A spurious match would make the node be declared ready to accept configuration before the SR OS control process is actually up, so configuration pushes could fail or race boot. This is a robustness concern, not a demonstrated defect: the container-internal process layout cannot be verified from this snapshot, and the intent of the change (likely matching a new binary path such as `/opt/nokia/cpm/...` in newer images) is reasonable. Note also that `pgrep -f` matches substrings, so a path like `/opt/nokia/cpmsomething` would also satisfy the `cpm` probe.

**Suggestion:** Anchor the patterns to the start of the command line so the match stays as precise as the originals, for example `` `/usr/bin/pgrep -f '^/opt/nokia/cpm'` `` (and the analogous `both`/`iom` variants). This is a one-token change per constant and preserves the intended full-path matching.

## Coverage notes

- Complete source-only review; no tests, builds, or container probes were executed (the review environment is read-only, so runtime behavior of `pgrep -f` inside SR-SIM images could not be verified).
- The changed constants are consumed only by `sros.Ready()`; a repository-wide `pgrep` search confirmed no other call sites depend on the old patterns.
- No unit tests cover the readiness probes (pre-existing gap; the probes depend on container internals and this is effectively a one-line constants change, so the ponytail rule that trivial one-liners need no test applies).
- No documentation or schema updates are warranted: the probe commands are internal implementation details not surfaced in `docs/manual/kinds/sros.md`, `docs/manual/kinds/vr-sros.md`, or `schemas/clab.schema.json`.
- The assumed image-side layout (`/opt/nokia/cpm`, `/opt/nokia/both`, `/opt/nokia/iom` appearing in process command lines) could not be confirmed from the snapshot; if, for instance, the actual `both`-mode binary does not live at `/opt/nokia/both`, that probe would never match and BOTH-mode nodes would fall back to the `cpm`/`iom` probes or time out after `readyTimeout`. This is flagged as uncertainty rather than a defect.
- No formatting issues were identified; no CI formatting evidence was supplied.
